page: Vultr vhf-2c-4gb is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the High Frequency Compute family. It features 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel core with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core) and includes a bundled 128 GB NVMe SSD for local storage.

Benchmark data indicates moderate single-core performance alongside weaker multi-core and memory capabilities. The single-core stress-ng performance of 1873.78 and Geekbench single-core score of 1456.0 both rank in the average tier. However, multi-core benchmarks are weak, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2405.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 3596.49. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with large-block read and write speeds falling into the bottom 10% tier at 22.81 GB/sec and 12.89 GB/sec respectively. Single-threaded gzip compression is a relative strength, scoring in the top 25% at 32.63 GB/sec.

Given its shared CPU allocation and modest memory capacity, this server type offers an entry-level resource density suitable for budget-conscious deployments. The presence of local NVMe SSD storage provides fast disk access, but the low database operation benchmark of 999.52 in PassMark and weak Redis SET performance of 2.61 million operations per second suggest it is not suited for high-throughput database workloads. It is best utilized for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic web serving, development environments, or small-scale utility tasks that do not require sustained multi-core compute or high memory bandwidth.
